references.text: Moses' song of praise poses the same rhetorical question about who is like the Lord among the gods, and praises his majesty and mighty deeds.
The psalmist declares that no one among the gods is like the Lord, and no deeds can compare with his, the same theme as in Deuteronomy.
The psalm praises the Lord's incomparable greatness in heaven and his power, reflecting Moses' confession of God's uniqueness.
God says that Moses will see what he will do to Pharaoh with a strong hand, the same expression used here.
Moses reminds the people of God's mighty deeds and strong hand that brought them out of Egypt.
A reference to the Lord's greatness, his strong hand, and his mighty deeds that the people have seen.
The Lord declares that he is God and there is none like him, the same unique divine claim.
Daniel confesses God's power that led the people out of Egypt with a strong hand, using the same language as Moses.
Nehemiah refers to the people whom God redeemed with his great power and strong hand.
